newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends down on lack of support.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends down on lack of support.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended the day lower with lack of leads and the closure of the Japanese markets having an impact on the market, dealers said.

"Today is Monday, and moreover the Japanese markets are closed, so there was basically no interest in the market," a dealer said.adding that most buyers are mostly sidelined because of ample supply in the market.
"Production is coming back to the market as rains has stopped in some main growing areas in Malaysia," a dealer said.
But dealers expect fresh demand to come back mainly from Europe as the summer holidays are over.
"Producers are quoting high levels but buyers are not willing to commit on expectation that prices may come down because of increasing raw materials," a dealer added.
At the close, October RSS 1 buyer fell three cents to 321.50 cents ($1.28) a kg and October SMR 20 buyer was down 1.50 cents at 311.50.

The INRO five-day average was 248.39 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Sept 20 from 248.99 on Sept 19. The daily indicator was 247.39 against 248.08. -- Tan Lee Lee (603-230-7510) ($1=2.5020 ringgit)
